title: Prime localization after finite purely inseparable scalar extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $E/k$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal of $R$. Put $R_E=R\otimes_kE$, $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, and $C=A\otimes_kE$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Tensor products have their usual algebra multiplication. The contraction map on prime ideals of $C$ to those of $A$ is a bijection respecting inclusion in both directions. In particular $C$ is a local ring, meaning a ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and $\mathfrak n$ is the unique prime of $C$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$. For every prime $\mathfrak P$ of $R_E$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$, the canonical map $R_E\to C$, $r\otimes e\mapsto(r/1)\otimes e$, has inverse image $\mathfrak P$ of $\mathfrak n$ and extends to a ring isomorphism
$$\theta_{\mathfrak P}:(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}\xrightarrow{\sim}C,\qquad t/u\longmapsto\overline t\,\overline u^{-1},$$
where bars denote images in $C$. This isomorphism is compatible with the maps from $R_E$ and $A$. It is also compatible with any map to a ring $D$ that inverts $R_E\setminus\mathfrak P$: the maps from $C$ and $(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}$ to $D$ induced by the same map $R_E\to D$ agree under $\theta_{\mathfrak P}$. No Noetherian, finite type or closed-point hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 035W (lemma-geometrically-reduced-at-point), first paragraph of proof: purely inseparable scalar extension is local and is the local ring at the unique point; uses algebra.tex Tag 0BRA (lemma-p-ring-map).

proof.text: For either $B=A$ or $B=R$, apply [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] to $\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the base-changed scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kE)$ and its projection is induced by $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Thus contraction is a homeomorphism, hence a bijection, on prime ideals. It preserves inclusion both ways: in the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $Q\subseteq Q\prime$ means $Q\prime\in\overline{\{Q\}}$, since this closure is $V(Q)$ (intersect the closed sets $V(I)$ containing $Q$). A homeomorphism and its inverse preserve these closures. In particular this proves the first assertion for $C$, and also uniqueness of a prime of $R_E$ over any given prime of $R$.

source.place: Tag 035W, lemma-geometrically-reduced-at-point, first proof paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 0BRA, lemma-p-ring-map

proof.text: The ring $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Every prime of $A$ is contained in $\mathfrak m$: use [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] and uniqueness of the maximal ideal. Let $\mathfrak n$ correspond to $\mathfrak m$ under step 1. Every prime of $C$ is contained in $\mathfrak n$. A maximal ideal containing the proper ideal $\mathfrak n$ exists by the same cited lemma; being prime (if $ab$ lies in a maximal ideal $M$ and $a$ does not, write $1=m+ca$ to deduce $b\in M$), it is contained in $\mathfrak n$, so equals it. Every maximal ideal of $C$ is likewise contained in $\mathfrak n$ and equals it. Thus $C$ is local and $\mathfrak n$ is its unique prime contracting to $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring, (1) and (2); Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, maximal-ideal existence

proof.text: Put $S=R_E$, $V=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, and $j:S\to C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with its base ring $k$, its algebra and module both $R$, its multiplicative subset $V$, and its second module $E$. It identifies $C$ with the module localization $V^{-1}S$ by $(r\otimes e)/v\mapsto(r/v)\otimes e$. This is also a ring identification: on generators the product is $((r\otimes e)/v)((r\prime\otimes e\prime)/w)=(rr\prime\otimes ee\prime)/(vw)$ on both sides, and the identity is preserved; distribute over finite sums. Equivalently, under $j$ each image of $v\in V$ is a unit with inverse $(1/v)\otimes1$, every element of $C$ has form $j(t)j(v\otimes1)^{-1}$, and $j(t)=0$ implies $(v\otimes1)t=0$ for some $v\in V$. Hence $C$ has the ring-localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] at these images of $V$.

source.place: Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization, and Tag 00D2, lemma-tensor-with-bimodule; Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak P\subset S$ contract to $\mathfrak p$. The inverse image $j^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is a prime ideal, since the inverse image of a proper prime under a unital ring map is proper and satisfies the prime-product condition. Its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak p$: the contraction of $\mathfrak n$ to $A$ is $\mathfrak m$, and [lem-trf-localization-maximal-contraction] identifies the contraction of $\mathfrak m$ to $R$ with $\mathfrak p$. By uniqueness over $\mathfrak p$ from step 1, $j^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak P$.

source.place: Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring, (1) and (3); Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization, existence and uniqueness

proof.text: The construction gives $\theta_{\mathfrak P}(t/1)=j(t)$ for $t\in S$, so it is compatible with $R_E$. On $A$ the structural map into $S_{\mathfrak P}$ sends $r/v$ to $(r\otimes1)/(v\otimes1)$; applying $\theta_{\mathfrak P}$ gives $(r/v)\otimes1$, proving compatibility with $A$. Finally let $f:S\to D$ invert $S\setminus\mathfrak P$. It inverts the images of $V$, so step 3 gives $f_C:C\to D$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] gives $f_{\mathfrak P}:S_{\mathfrak P}\to D$. The maps $f_C\theta_{\mathfrak P}$ and $f_{\mathfrak P}$ agree on $S$, hence are equal by the same uniqueness assertion. This includes arbitrary $D$ and completes every compatibility clause.
